objective: Add a search language for the catalogue in a new module `stockroom/query.py`, for example `tag:gift price<20 -name:"blue mug" OR sku:TEA-*`. Syntax tree: frozen dataclasses (compared by value) `Term(field, op, value)` (`field` is `None` for a plain word, else one of `sku`, `name`, `tag`, `price`, `reorder`; `op` is `:` for plain words), `Not(child)`, `And(children)` and `Or(children)` (`children` a tuple). Errors are `QueryError(ParseError)` (a subclass of `stockroom.errors.ParseError`) with an attribute `column` (1-based character position in the text) and the message `column C: REASON`. `parse_query(text)`: whitespace is any character for which `str.isspace()` is true (so U+00A0 and U+2028 too). A quoted string is `"` ... `"` with `""` standing for one `"`; after its closing quote the next character must be whitespace, `)` or the end of the text (any other character is an error at that character's column, so `"a"b` is an error at column 4). A word is a maximal run of characters other than whitespace, `(`, `)` and `"` (so parentheses need no spaces around them). The word `OR` (exactly, upper case, not quoted) is the operator, also when `(` or `"` follows it directly (`a OR"b"` is `Or((a, b))`); everything else is an operand. A word without any of `:` `<` `>` is a plain term `Term(None, ':', word)`, and a quoted string on its own is `Term(None, ':', content)`. Otherwise the text before the first of `:` `<` `>` is the field, which must be one of the five names (lower case; anything else, including an empty name, is an error at the word's first column); the operator is `:`, `<`, `<=`, `>` or `>=` (a `<` or `>` directly followed by `=` is `<=` or `>=`), and `sku`, `name` and `tag` allow only `:` (another operator is an error at the operator's column); the rest of the word is the value, which may not contain `:`, `<` or `>` (error at that character). When the rest is empty, a quoted string must follow directly (no space) and is the value; otherwise it is an error at the column where the value would start. A `price` value must be ASCII digits optionally followed by `.` and one or two digits, a `reorder` value ASCII digits only, otherwise an error at the value's first column (its opening quote when quoted). A `"` directly after any other word is an error at that quote. Within one word the checks run in this order, and the first failing one is reported: the field name, the operator, a `:` `<` `>` in the value, a missing value (or, for a quoted value, its own errors: unterminated, or a wrong character after its closing quote), a `"` directly after the word, and last the `price` or `reorder` value format (so `price:12.345"x"` is an error at the quote, column 13). Grammar: a query is alternatives joined by `OR`; an alternative is one or more units side by side (an implicit AND, which binds tighter than `OR`); a unit is an operand, `( query )`, or `-` directly followed by a unit (`Not`). A `-` that is not directly followed by `(`, `"` or a character that can start a word other than `-` (that is: followed by whitespace, `)`, `-` or the end) is an error at the `-`. Where a unit is expected but `OR`, `)` or the end of the text comes, it is an error at that `OR` or `)`, or at column `len(text) + 1` for the end; so `()` is an error at its `)`. A `(` without its `)` is an error at column `len(text) + 1`, and a `)` without its `(` is an error at that `)`. An unterminated quoted string is an error at its opening quote. The tree is normalised: an AND or OR of one unit is that unit itself, parentheses leave no node of their own, and an `And` directly inside an `And` (or an `Or` inside an `Or`) is replaced by its children in place (`(a b) c` is `And((a, b, c))`, `(a OR b) OR c` is `Or((a, b, c))`); `Not` is never removed (`-(-a)` is `Not(Not(a))`). A text that is empty or only whitespace is `And(())`. `format_query(node)` writes the canonical text: a value is written as it is when it is not empty, is not `OR`, does not start with `-` and contains no whitespace and none of `" ( ) < > :`; otherwise it is quoted with `"` doubled. A `Term` is `field + op + value` (just the value for a plain term); `Not` is `-` before a term, otherwise `-(` + inner + `)`; `And` joins its children with one space, putting an `Or` child in parentheses; `Or` joins its children with ` OR ` (no parentheses around `And` children); `And(())` is `''`. For every normalised tree `parse_query(format_query(node)) == node`. `matches(node, item) -> bool` for a `stockroom.models.Item`, comparing text after `str.casefold()` (so `strasse` finds `Straße`): a plain term matches when its value is a substring of the name or of the SKU; `name:` is a substring of the name; `tag:` equals one of the tags; `sku:` is a pattern over the whole SKU where `*` matches any run of characters (also none), `?` exactly one character, and every other character (including `[`) only itself; `price` compares the price in cents with the value read as an amount (`12.5` is 1250) and `reorder` compares `reorder_level`, `:` meaning equal; `Not`, `And` (all children; `And(())` matches everything) and `Or` (any child) combine as usual. Finally add `--where QUERY` to `python -m stockroom items`: only items that match are listed, in file order (it combines with `--tag`; an empty query lists everything). A bad query exits with code 1, `stockroom: error: ` followed by the `QueryError` message on stderr, and empty stdout. Existing behaviour otherwise stays.
acceptance: `parse_query` builds the stated trees: `And(())` for empty or blank text, plain words, quoted strings with doubled quotes and the empty string, field terms with every allowed operator, quoted field values that contain `:` `<` `>`, `-` before terms, quoted strings and groups, `OR` with lower precedence than juxtaposition, flattening of nested `And`/`Or` and of parentheses, `Not(Not(a))` for `-(-a)`, groups without surrounding spaces (`(a)b`, `a(b)`), `OR` directly followed by `"` or `(` (`a OR"b"`, `a OR(b c)`), `or`, `and` and `ORx` as ordinary words, a quoted `"OR"` as a term, `-` inside words and values, U+00A0 and U+2028 as whitespace, and non-ASCII words

Errors are `QueryError` (a `ParseError`) with the message `column C: ...` and the column of each stated rule, for 54 texts: unterminated quotes (`"abc` at 1, `name:"abc` at 6), characters after a closing quote (`"a"b` and `"a"(b)` at 4), a quote after a word (`ab"c"` at 3), a `-` before a space, the end, `-` or `)`, `OR` where a unit is expected (`OR a` at 1, `a OR OR b` at 6, `a -OR b` at 4), the end where a unit is expected (`a OR` at 5), `()` at 2, a missing `)` at `len + 1`, a stray `)`, unknown fields (`colour`, empty, `Name`, `price=`), operators not allowed for the field (`name<x` at 5), a second `<` in the value (`price<<5` at 7), `:` in a value, a missing value (also before a space), and bad `price` and `reorder` values (`12.345`, `1,000`, `-5`, `.5`, `5.`, an Arabic-Indic digit, `²`, `1_000`, a quoted `"12 "`, `1.5` and `1_0` for reorder) at the value's column, and the stated order of checks inside one word (`price:1:2` at 8, `price:12.345"x"` at 13, `reorder:"x"y` at 12, `colour:"x` at 1, `name<"x` at 5)

`format_query` writes `''`, bare and quoted values by the stated rule (`"blue mug"`, `"say ""hi"""`, `""`, `"OR"`, `ORx`, `"-x"`, `a-b`, `"a:b"`, `"(a)"`, a value with U+00A0 quoted), `price<=12.5`, `name:"blue mug"`, `name:"-x"`, `tag:""`, `-tag:gift`, `-"a b"`, `-(a b)`, `-(-a)`, `a (b OR c) -d`, `a b OR c`, `-(a OR b) OR c`, and the canonical text `tag:gift (a OR b) -c` for a messy query

For 3,000 seeded random normalised trees (depth up to 3; values from letters, digits, spaces, tabs, U+00A0, quotes, parentheses, `: < > - = * ?`, `é`, `ß`, `OR`; valid price and reorder values; every operator): `parse_query(format_query(node)) == node`, formatting the parsed tree gives the same text, and extra whitespace around `OR` and parentheses does not change the tree

`matches` follows the rules on a fixed catalogue: case folding (`MUG`, `strasse`, `name:STRASSE`, `name:straße`, `cafÉ`), plain words searching name and SKU (`tea-0` finds `TEA-010` but `name:tea-0` nothing), exact tags (`tag:KITCHEN`, not `tag:kit`), SKU patterns (`MUG-*`, `mug-00?`, `*1*`, not `MUG`, `[` literal), price and reorder comparisons with every operator (`12.5` equals `12.50`, `1000.98`), negated groups, double negation, the empty query and `""` matching everything, and `tag:""` matching nothing

For 1,500 seeded random trees (plus random `sku:` patterns of `M u g - 0 1 * ? A`) and 40 seeded random items (names with `ß`, `SS`, `é`, `É`, quotes, parentheses, `*`, `?`; tags such as `Gift`, `straße`, `a b`), `matches` equals the stated rules evaluated independently, also for the tree parsed back from `format_query`

`python -m stockroom items --file F --where Q` lists the matching items in file order (`mug`, `name:strasse`, `tag:gift OR price<7`, `-(tag:kitchen OR tag:food) reorder>=5`, `name:"green tea"`, an empty result, the empty query listing everything, `--where` together with `--tag`), and a bad query (`tag:gift (`, `colour:red`, `name:"x`, `price<12.345`) exits with code 1, empty stdout and stderr starting `stockroom: error: column C: ` with the column of the error (11, 1, 6, 7)
